---
title: "Holly Candidates"
subtitle: "Small, isolated evergreen crowns in leaf-off imagery as candidate holly locations"
date: today
---

```{r setup}
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(leaflet)
library(plotly)
library(terra)
library(here)

source(here("R", "functions.R"))
derived <- here(cfg$paths$derived)
h <- cfg$holly

line    <- load_transect()
windows <- load_windows()
obj     <- holly_candidates(load_holly_objects())
gli_path <- file.path(derived, "holly_objects_gli.gpkg")   # first pass, RGB only (GLI)
obj_gli <- if (file.exists(gli_path)) holly_candidates(st_read(gli_path, quiet = TRUE)) else NULL
cal_path <- file.path(derived, "ndvi_calibration.csv")
cal     <- if (file.exists(cal_path)) read.csv(cal_path) else NULL
classes <- read.csv(file.path(derived, "nlcd_window_classes.csv"))
nlcd    <- read.csv(file.path(derived, "nlcd_windows.csv"))

vi_name <- unique(obj$vi_name)
vi_label <- c(gli = "GLI (green leaf index, RGB)", ndvi = "NDVI (near-infrared)")[vi_name]
thr <- h$thresholds[[vi_name]]

reason_cols <- c(candidate = "#d95f02", `not isolated` = "#7570b3",
                 `developed/water` = "#999999", size = "#cccccc")
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Candidates now use NDVI

The candidates on this page come from NDVI computed from the 4-band (RGB + near-infrared)
imagery. The first pass used the RGB-only green leaf index (GLI); its results are kept for
comparison in [GLI versus NDVI](#gli-versus-ndvi). Candidates are still unverified: until
field data exist, they are locations to visit, not holly.
:::

## Purpose

American holly (*Ilex opaca*) is evergreen, so in leaf-off imagery (flown February to March
2025) its crowns stay green while the deciduous canopy around it is bare. This page builds the
first step of a holly classification workflow:

1. **Candidates from imagery** (this page): find small, isolated evergreen crowns in
   non-developed areas.
2. **Ground truth**: visit candidate locations and record what is there (holly, sex if known,
   or the false-positive species).
3. **Classification**: train a supervised classifier on crown features (including NDVI and
   NIR) using the field labels, then map holly across the transect.

| Step | Script | Output |
|---|---|---|
| 7. Crown extraction | `R/06_holly_objects.R` | `data/derived/holly_objects.gpkg` (all crowns with features) |
| 8. Candidate rule | `holly_candidates()` in `R/functions.R` | `data/derived/holly_candidates.{csv,gpx}` (field list) |

Greenness comes from NDVI. The mosaic is built from the 4-band tiles, and `veg_index()`
uses NDVI whenever the imagery has a `nir` band (GLI otherwise). Every crown also records its
mean GLI, so the two indices can be compared on the same objects.

## Why NDVI

Healthy leaves treat red and near-infrared (NIR) light very differently. Chlorophyll absorbs
most red light for photosynthesis, while the internal cell structure of a leaf (the spongy
mesophyll) scatters and reflects most NIR light. Bare branches, dead or dormant grass, soil,
and pavement show much less of this contrast. The normalized difference vegetation index
captures it in one number:

$$
\text{NDVI} = \frac{\text{NIR} - \text{Red}}{\text{NIR} + \text{Red}}
$$

NDVI ranges from −1 to 1. Water is negative, soil, rock, and pavement sit near 0, and dense
green foliage is typically above 0.6. Because it is a ratio, it is also less sensitive to
illumination than a single band, so a shaded crown and a sunlit crown of the same tree give
similar values.

This contrast is what makes leaf-off imagery useful for holly. In February and March the
deciduous canopy is bare and has low NDVI, while evergreen foliage stays green and has high
NDVI. Holly in the understory should stand out clearly against the bare hardwoods around it.

The RGB stand-in used for the first pass, the green leaf index (GLI), relies only on the small
green reflectance peak of leaves in visible light. In this imagery GLI separates pine canopy
(median about 0.03) from leaf-off hardwood (about −0.01) by only a narrow margin. It is also
affected by shadows and by the imagery's slight blue cast.

### Separation in this imagery

To compare the two indices and set the NDVI thresholds, both were computed (3 × 3 px
smoothed, as in crown extraction) at `r if (!is.null(cal)) format(nrow(cal), big.mark = ",")`
random points in the study area and grouped by NLCD class. NLCD is a 30 m product, so these
labels are noisy at 1 ft (a "deciduous" cell can contain a pine), which blurs both indices
equally.

```{r calibration, eval=!is.null(cal)}
auc <- function(neg, pos) {
  r <- rank(c(neg, pos))
  (sum(r[length(neg) + seq_along(pos)]) - length(pos) * (length(pos) + 1) / 2) /
    (length(neg) * length(pos))
}
dec <- cal[cal$nlcd == 41, ]
evg <- cal[cal$nlcd == 42, ]
cal_tab <- data.frame(
  Index = c("GLI (RGB)", "NDVI (NIR)"),
  dec = c(median(dec$gli), median(dec$ndvi)),
  evg = c(median(evg$gli), median(evg$ndvi)),
  crown = c(h$thresholds$gli$crown, h$thresholds$ndvi$crown),
  dec_over = c(mean(dec$gli > h$thresholds$gli$crown), mean(dec$ndvi > h$thresholds$ndvi$crown)),
  evg_over = c(mean(evg$gli > h$thresholds$gli$crown), mean(evg$ndvi > h$thresholds$ndvi$crown)),
  auc = c(auc(dec$gli, evg$gli), auc(dec$ndvi, evg$ndvi))
)
knitr::kable(cal_tab, digits = c(0, 3, 3, 2, 3, 3, 2),
             col.names = c("Index", "Median, deciduous (41)", "Median, evergreen (42)",
                           "Crown threshold", "Deciduous above", "Evergreen above", "AUC"))
```

```{r calibration-plot, eval=!is.null(cal), fig.width=9, fig.height=3.6}
cal |>
  filter(nlcd %in% c(21, 41, 42)) |>
  mutate(cover = factor(nlcd, c(41, 42, 21),
                        c("Deciduous forest (41)", "Evergreen forest (42)", "Developed, open (21)"))) |>
  pivot_longer(c(gli, ndvi), names_to = "index") |>
  mutate(index = toupper(index)) |>
  ggplot(aes(value, colour = cover, fill = cover)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.15, linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_vline(data = data.frame(index = c("GLI", "NDVI"),
                               v = c(h$thresholds$gli$crown, h$thresholds$ndvi$crown)),
             aes(xintercept = v), linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~index, scales = "free") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#b5651d", "#1b7837", "#999999"), name = NULL) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#b5651d", "#1b7837", "#999999"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Index (dashed line: crown threshold)", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "top", axis.text.y = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

AUC is the probability that a random evergreen-forest point has a higher index than a random
deciduous-forest point (0.5 = no separation, 1 = complete). NDVI separates the two forest types
much better than GLI. Absolute NDVI is high even in leaf-off hardwood (median about 0.33)
because the imagery's NIR band is not radiometrically calibrated and bare branches over
leaf litter still reflect NIR. Only relative values matter here.

The NDVI thresholds were chosen to match the GLI rule's false-positive rate on deciduous
forest. The crown threshold (`r h$thresholds$ndvi$crown`) is exceeded by about 2% of
deciduous-forest pixels, as GLI's `r h$thresholds$gli$crown` is, and the context threshold
(`r h$thresholds$ndvi$context`) by about 9–10%, as GLI's `r h$thresholds$gli$context` is.
At the same false-positive rate, NDVI keeps far more of the evergreen canopy above threshold.

### Measuring the gain from NIR

Every crown carries both GLI and NDVI means (`gli_mean`, `ndvi_mean`) along with NIR
reflectance. Once field labels exist, the comparison will use the same ground-truth set and the
same spatially blocked cross-validation for two classifiers:

- **Visible only:** crown features from RGB (GLI, colour, brightness, size, shape, isolation).
- **Visible + NIR:** the same features plus NDVI and NIR reflectance.

The improvement will be reported as the change in precision (share of candidates that are
holly), recall (share of holly found), and overall accuracy, along with how many candidates
drop out of the field list.

## Approach

Each 12-inch tile is processed at full resolution:

1. **Vegetation index** (`r vi_label`), smoothed with a `r h$smooth_px` × `r h$smooth_px` px mean.
2. **Crowns:** pixels with index > `r thr$crown` are evergreen crown; connected groups of them
   are crown objects. Objects `r h$extract_diam_ft[1]`–`r h$extract_diam_ft[2]` ft across
   (equivalent-circle diameter) are kept with their features.
3. **Isolation:** the share of evergreen pixels (index > `r thr$context`, a lower threshold) in
   the `r h$context_window * h$context_cell_px` ft neighbourhood of each crown. Holly in a
   leaf-off hardwood stand has a low share; a crown inside pine canopy has a high one.
4. **Candidate rule:** crown `r h$candidate_diam_ft[1]`–`r h$candidate_diam_ft[2]` ft across,
   evergreen share ≤ `r h$context_max`, and NLCD class not water or developed
   (`r paste(h$exclude_nlcd, collapse = ", ")`). Crowns cut by a tile edge are excluded from
   the field list.

Thresholds are calibrated on NLCD forest classes (see [Separation in this
imagery](#separation-in-this-imagery)).

### Example

A 600 × 600 ft area 22.5 km along the transect: a pine stand (upper left) next to leaf-off
hardwoods (lower right). Candidates are the isolated crowns in the hardwood stand; crowns
inside the pine canopy are rejected as not isolated.

```{r example, fig.width=10, fig.height=5.2}
ends <- st_coordinates(line)[, 1:2]
d <- (ends[2, ] - ends[1, ]) / sqrt(sum((ends[2, ] - ends[1, ])^2))
p <- ends[1, ] + km_to_crs(22.5) * d
e <- ext(p[1] - 300, p[1] + 300, p[2] - 300, p[2] + 300)
chip <- crop(load_ortho(aoi = FALSE), e)
names(chip) <- band_names(chip)
vi <- focal(veg_index(chip, vi_name), h$smooth_px, "mean", na.policy = "omit")
ex <- obj[st_as_sf(as.polygons(e, crs = crs(chip))), ]
ex <- ex[ex$reason %in% c("candidate", "not isolated"), ]

par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(0.5, 0.5, 2, 0.5))
plotRGB(chip, mar = c(0.5, 0.5, 2, 0.5)); title("Imagery with crowns")
plot(vect(ex), add = TRUE, border = reason_cols[ex$reason], lwd = 2)
legend("bottomleft", c("candidate", "not isolated"), col = reason_cols[c("candidate", "not isolated")],
       lwd = 2, bg = "white", cex = 0.8)
plot(vi, main = vi_label, axes = FALSE, legend = TRUE, mar = c(0.5, 0.5, 2, 4),
     col = hcl.colors(50, "Greens 3", rev = TRUE))
```

## Candidates

```{r counts}
n_tot <- nrow(obj)
n_cand <- sum(obj$candidate & !obj$tile_edge)
obj |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  mutate(reason = factor(reason, levels = names(reason_cols))) |>
  count(reason, name = "crowns") |>
  mutate(share = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * crowns / sum(crowns))) |>
  knitr::kable(col.names = c("Rule outcome", "Crowns", "Share"),
               format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

Of `r format(n_tot, big.mark = ",")` evergreen crowns `r h$extract_diam_ft[1]`–`r h$extract_diam_ft[2]` ft
across in the study area, **`r format(n_cand, big.mark = ",")`** pass the candidate rule (the
outcome is the first rule a crown fails). Zoom in on the map to see individual candidates over
the imagery; click one for its id and features.

```{r map}
cand <- obj[obj$candidate & !obj$tile_edge, ]
cand_ll <- st_transform(st_centroid(cand), 4326)
cand_ll$popup <- sprintf(
  "<b>%s</b><br>%.0f ft crown<br>%s %.3f<br>Evergreen share: %.2f<br>Window %d (%.1f km)<br>%.6f, %.6f",
  cand_ll$obj_id, cand_ll$diam_ft, toupper(vi_name), cand_ll$vi_mean, cand_ll$context,
  cand_ll$window, cand_ll$u_km, cand_ll$lat, cand_ll$lon
)

leaflet(cand_ll) |>
  addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldImagery, group = "Imagery",
                   options = providerTileOptions(maxNativeZoom = 19, maxZoom = 21)) |>
  addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldGrayCanvas, group = "Light") |>
  addPolylines(data = st_transform(line, 4326), color = "white", dashArray = "6", weight = 2) |>
  addCircleMarkers(radius = 5, color = "#d95f02", weight = 2, fillOpacity = 0.3,
                   popup = ~popup, clusterOptions = markerClusterOptions(disableClusteringAtZoom = 18)) |>
  addLayersControl(baseGroups = c("Imagery", "Light"))
```

### Along the transect

Candidate density per km² of non-developed land (NLCD classes other than
`r paste(h$exclude_nlcd, collapse = ", ")`) in each 1 km window, with the window's forest cover
for reference.

```{r density}
nondev <- classes |>
  filter(!class %in% h$exclude_nlcd) |>
  group_by(window) |>
  summarise(nondev_frac = sum(frac))
dens <- windows |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  left_join(nondev, by = "window") |>
  left_join(count(st_drop_geometry(cand), window, name = "n"), by = "window") |>
  left_join(select(nlcd, window, forest_pct), by = "window") |>
  mutate(n = coalesce(n, 0L),
         nondev_km2 = area_km2 * nondev_frac,
         per_km2 = ifelse(nondev_km2 > 0.05, n / nondev_km2, NA))

plot_ly(dens, x = ~u_mid_km) |>
  add_bars(y = ~per_km2, name = "Candidates per km² non-developed",
           marker = list(color = "#d95f02"),
           customdata = ~sprintf("%d candidates in %.2f km²", n, nondev_km2),
           hovertemplate = "%{y:.0f} per km² (%{customdata})<extra></extra>") |>
  layout(xaxis = list(title = "Distance from Richmond (km)", dtick = 5),
         yaxis = list(title = "Candidates per km²"),
         hovermode = "x unified", showlegend = FALSE) |>
  config(displaylogo = FALSE)
```

### Candidate gallery

A random sample of candidates, 60 × 60 ft around each crown (outlined), for a quick visual
check of what the rule picks up.

```{r gallery, fig.width=10, fig.height=7}
set.seed(2025)
ortho <- load_ortho(aoi = FALSE)
samp <- cand[sample(nrow(cand), min(24, nrow(cand))), ]
par(mfrow = c(4, 6), mar = c(0.2, 0.2, 1.2, 0.2))
for (i in seq_len(nrow(samp))) {
  ctr <- st_coordinates(st_centroid(st_geometry(samp[i, ])))
  x <- crop(ortho, ext(ctr[1] - 30, ctr[1] + 30, ctr[2] - 30, ctr[2] + 30))
  plotRGB(x[[1:3]], mar = c(0.2, 0.2, 1.2, 0.2))
  plot(vect(samp[i, ]), add = TRUE, border = "#d95f02", lwd = 1.5)
  where <- if (is.na(samp$window[i])) "end cap" else sprintf("window %d", samp$window[i])
  title(sprintf("%.0f ft, %s", samp$diam_ft[i], where), cex.main = 0.8, line = 0.2)
}
```

### Crown features

Features recorded for every crown, compared between candidates and crowns rejected as not
isolated (mostly crowns within pine or other evergreen canopy). These are the starting inputs
for the classifier.

```{r features, fig.width=9, fig.height=6}
obj |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  filter(reason %in% c("candidate", "not isolated")) |>
  select(reason, `Diameter (ft)` = diam_ft, Compactness = compactness,
         `NDVI mean` = ndvi_mean, `GLI mean` = gli_mean, NIR = nir,
         Brightness = brightness, `Evergreen share` = context) |>
  pivot_longer(-reason) |>
  ggplot(aes(value, fill = reason, colour = reason)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.25, linewidth = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free", nrow = 2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = reason_cols, name = NULL) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = reason_cols, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "top", axis.text.y = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

## GLI versus NDVI

```{r compare-setup, eval=!is.null(obj_gli)}
cand_gli <- obj_gli[obj_gli$candidate & !obj_gli$tile_edge, ]
match_ft <- 10    # a candidate "matches" one from the other run if their centres are this close
near <- function(a, b) lengths(st_is_within_distance(st_centroid(st_geometry(a)),
                                                     st_centroid(st_geometry(b)), match_ft)) > 0
gli_kept  <- near(cand_gli, cand)     # GLI candidates also found with NDVI
ndvi_seen <- near(cand, cand_gli)     # NDVI candidates also found with GLI
cmp <- data.frame(
  Measure = c("Crowns extracted (6–30 ft)", "Candidates (field list)",
              sprintf("Candidates also found by the other index (within %d ft)", match_ft),
              "Median candidate diameter (ft)", "Median evergreen share around candidates"),
  GLI = c(format(nrow(obj_gli), big.mark = ","), format(nrow(cand_gli), big.mark = ","),
          sprintf("%s (%.0f%%)", format(sum(gli_kept), big.mark = ","), 100 * mean(gli_kept)),
          sprintf("%.1f", median(cand_gli$diam_ft)), sprintf("%.2f", median(cand_gli$context))),
  NDVI = c(format(nrow(obj), big.mark = ","), format(nrow(cand), big.mark = ","),
           sprintf("%s (%.0f%%)", format(sum(ndvi_seen), big.mark = ","), 100 * mean(ndvi_seen)),
           sprintf("%.1f", median(cand$diam_ft)), sprintf("%.2f", median(cand$context)))
)
```

The same crown extraction and candidate rule, run once with GLI (RGB only) and once with NDVI
(4-band), with thresholds matched on deciduous-forest false positives.

```{r compare-table, eval=!is.null(obj_gli)}
knitr::kable(cmp, align = "lrr")
```

```{r compare-reasons, eval=!is.null(obj_gli)}
bind_rows(GLI = st_drop_geometry(obj_gli)[, "reason", drop = FALSE],
          NDVI = st_drop_geometry(obj)[, "reason", drop = FALSE], .id = "index") |>
  mutate(reason = factor(reason, levels = names(reason_cols))) |>
  count(index, reason) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = index, values_from = n) |>
  knitr::kable(col.names = c("Rule outcome", "GLI crowns", "NDVI crowns"),
               format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

```{r compare-density, eval=!is.null(obj_gli)}
dens_gli <- count(st_drop_geometry(cand_gli), window, name = "n_gli")
cmp_dens <- dens |>
  left_join(dens_gli, by = "window") |>
  mutate(n_gli = coalesce(n_gli, 0L),
         gli_km2 = ifelse(nondev_km2 > 0.05, n_gli / nondev_km2, NA))

plot_ly(cmp_dens, x = ~u_mid_km) |>
  add_trace(y = ~gli_km2, type = "scatter", mode = "lines+markers", name = "GLI (RGB)",
            line = list(color = "#999999", width = 2), marker = list(color = "#999999", size = 7),
            hovertemplate = "GLI: %{y:.0f} per km²<extra></extra>") |>
  add_trace(y = ~per_km2, type = "scatter", mode = "lines+markers", name = "NDVI (4-band)",
            line = list(color = "#d95f02", width = 2), marker = list(color = "#d95f02", size = 7),
            hovertemplate = "NDVI: %{y:.0f} per km²<extra></extra>") |>
  layout(xaxis = list(title = "Distance from Richmond (km)", dtick = 5, hoverformat = ".1f"),
         yaxis = list(title = "Candidates per km² non-developed", rangemode = "tozero"),
         hovermode = "x unified", legend = list(orientation = "h", y = -0.2)) |>
  config(displaylogo = FALSE)
```

COMPARE_TEXT

## Ground truth

The field list is `data/derived/holly_candidates.csv` (with a GPX copy for GPS units and phone
apps). Each row has the crown id, latitude and longitude, transect position, crown diameter, and
the features used by the rule. Suggested field record per visited candidate:

| Field | Values |
|---|---|
| `obj_id` | crown id from the list (or new id for holly found nearby but not listed) |
| `species` | *Ilex opaca*, or the false positive (e.g. eastern red cedar, pine, magnolia, privet, ivy-covered trunk, lawn) |
| `sex` | female (fruit), male, unknown |
| `dbh_cm`, `height_m` | optional size measures |
| `notes`, `photo` | free text and photo id |

Crown ids are tied to the current thresholds; if the rule or index changes, match field records
to crowns by location rather than id. Keep field data outside `data/derived/` (for example
`data/field/`), since derived files are rebuilt by the scripts.

## Next steps

- **Sampling design:** a stratified random sample of candidates per window (or per NLCD
  class), so the field effort covers the full gradient.
- **Classifier:** with field labels, fit a supervised model (e.g. random forest) on crown
  features, validated with spatially blocked cross-validation (hold out whole windows).
- **Threshold check:** once field data exist, check the NDVI thresholds against crowns of
  known holly (the current values are calibrated on NLCD forest classes, not on holly).

## Notes

- **Expected false positives:** other evergreens of similar size, such as eastern red cedar,
  young loblolly or Virginia pine, southern magnolia, and evergreen shrubs (privet, *Elaeagnus*,
  mountain laurel), plus green ground cover such as winter grass or English ivy on trunks.
- **What is missed:** holly under evergreen canopy (hidden), crowns smaller than
  `r h$candidate_diam_ft[1]` ft, holly in developed areas (excluded by design), and crowns merged
  with neighbouring evergreens into one larger object.
- **Shadows:** the imagery has long shadows in places. NDVI is a ratio, so it is less affected
  than GLI, but deep shadow lowers both bands to near the noise level and makes NDVI unreliable
  there.
- **Winter lawns:** cool-season grass is green in February and March and has high NDVI. Lawns
  are mostly removed by the NLCD rule (developed classes) and by crown size and shape.
